title: Clutch Actuator Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the clutch actuator, which engages and releases the clutch automatically on automated manual and dual-clutch transmissions.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Jerky take-off or slipping clutch
Car may not move or may refuse to shift

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the clutch actuator
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the clutch actuator for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the clutch actuator against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the clutch actuator.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The clutch actuator is giving readings that don't match what the computer expects for the current conditions. The clutch actuator engages and releases the clutch automatically on automated manual and dual-clutch transmissions.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Jerky take-off or slipping clutch
Car may not move or may refuse to shift

causes.name: Worn clutch or clutch needing a relearn
High resistance in the wiring or connector
Control module software needs an update

checks: Compare the clutch actuator reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the clutch actuator.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the clutch actuator circuit that is lower than it should be. The clutch actuator engages and releases the clutch automatically on automated manual and dual-clutch transmissions.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Jerky take-off or slipping clutch
Car may not move or may refuse to shift

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the clutch actuator circuit

checks: Inspect the clutch actuator wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the clutch actuator and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the clutch actuator.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the clutch actuator circuit that is higher than it should be. The clutch actuator engages and releases the clutch automatically on automated manual and dual-clutch transmissions.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the clutch actuator circuit
Wire shorted to another power circuit

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the clutch actuator circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the clutch actuator against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the clutch actuator.

title: Gate Select Position Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the gate select position sensor keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire.

title: Gate Select Control Error

Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low hydraulic pressure on hydraulic systems

checks: Scan for actuator and sensor codes
Run the shift system relearn with a scan tool
fix: Relearn the system; if it returns, repair the actuator or binding shift mechanism.

Check engine light on

drive: Always set the parking brake when you park, and keep your foot on the brake when you shift. The shifter may come out of Park without the brake pressed or may get stuck in Park. Book a repair soon.
